title: the project declares its setup and checks; the gates stop hard-coding this repo's toolchain
acceptance: firstmate-workflow is meant to orchestrate work on other repositories too, so nothing in bin/ may assume this repository's own toolchain. Today fm-gate.sh gate 3 requires ./bin/ci.sh and passes FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS, which only this repo's ci.sh understands. Gate 5 classifies tests by fixed globs and runs only *.test.sh with bash. And every fresh worktree lacks this repo's gitignored node_modules, so its ci.sh silently skips e2e. The captain chose to make everything project-specific declared rather than coded. This task's own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

config.yaml gains a `project:` block that the target project fills in: `setup` (optional shell command preparing a fresh checkout, e.g. installing dependencies); `check` (required shell command whose exit status means green); `check_env` (optional map of environment variables for `check`); `tests` (optional list of globs classifying test files); `test` (optional command template containing `{file}` that runs one test file). bin/fm-config.sh exposes these values without evaluating them at read time. Values are opaque shell command strings; nothing in bin/ names bun, playwright, chromium, ci.sh or FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS.

fm-gate.sh: gate 3 runs `setup` (when declared) and then `check` with `check_env` in its detached worktree. If `check` is undeclared, gate 3 fails with a message saying config.yaml declares no project.check. If `setup` fails, gate 3 fails and names the failure; it never passes with a stage silently skipped because setup did not run. Gate 5 classifies test files using `tests` (defaulting to the current globs only when undeclared) and runs `setup` first. With the implementation reverted, it runs each changed test through `test` when declared, otherwise the whole `check`, and requires red.

`bin/fm-session.sh start` runs `setup` once for the repository checkout when declared and reports a `project` block in its JSON: which keys are declared, and the setup's observed exit status and a short error when it fails. A failed setup is reported as not ready and never aborts the rest of startup. `status` reports the declared contract read-only and never runs setup. With no setup declared, nothing is run.

This repository declares its own values in config.yaml: setup `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bunx playwright install chromium`, check `bin/ci.sh`, check_env FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS=600, and its current test globs and runner. Its local gate 3 therefore actually runs the end-to-end stage. README.md documents the `project:` block with at least two non-JavaScript examples (for instance a Go and a Python project) and a project with no setup.

skills/firstmate/SKILL.md: startup reports the project contract, and any fresh verification worktree runs the declared `setup` before `check`. A check whose output says a stage was skipped is not evidence that the stage passed.

Fail-first tests with no network, using fixture repos with their own config.yaml: gate 3 runs the declared check and setup (and fails loudly on setup failure or missing check); gate 5 honours `tests` globs and the `test` template on a fixture that is not a bash project; session start runs setup once and reports a failure without aborting; status never runs setup; config parsing keeps quotes, `&&` and `{file}` intact. Evidence is the pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates; this task does not require the worker to execute tests itself.

Captain decision D-051 = A: the project contract gains `docs`, an optional list of globs. Gate 5 needs no new test when every changed non-test path matches `docs`; any other non-test path still needs one; when `docs` is undeclared nothing is exempt. This repository declares `design/**` and `README.md`; skills are behaviour and are not docs. Fail-first tests: a docs-only diff passes gate 5, docs plus code without a test fails, and undeclared `docs` exempts nothing.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
